title: The Hum of the Border
story:
James stood before the Outer Fence, his fingers tracing the cold, rough wood of a post. The wire above him hummed with a low, vibrating life that he had never sensed in the Great Canopy. He had never felt a silence so thick with potential; he had never felt a wind so heavy with the scent of distant burning wood; he had never felt a curiosity so sharp it made his own fur prickle.

To calm his fluttering heart, James closed his eyes and began his grounding ritual. He counted the steady drone of the wire, the rhythmic scratching of dry grass against his toes, and the faint, rhythmic ticking coming from somewhere deep within the town structures. He took a steadying breath, bowed his head toward the sprawling, rigid landscape of the human world, and murmured, 'Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next.'

He noticed a gap beneath the fence where the soil had eroded away, leaving just enough room for a curious traveler to pass. Before he moved, he looked down at the heavy metal ring in his palm, feeling its solid, grounding weight. He wondered if this ring had once been a part of this fence, or perhaps a part of the buried spines that had guided him all the way from the hillside. The connection felt ancient and heavy, a mystery he wasn't quite ready to solve.

With a final glance at the oily reflection in the puddle—a distorted image of a creature who had once feared the edge of the trees—James ducked his head low and squeezed through the gap beneath the fence. He emerged on the other side, stepping onto gravel that crunched loudly beneath his feet, a sound so unnatural it felt like he was walking on a carpet of tiny, broken stars.
